_comment: The same twelfth-tell pass as data/voice_curate_12th.json, written out in exact
markup. `--curate` refuses an entry whose span crosses a tag - the words are the
same but the `find` has to carry the `<strong>` - and those refusals are the
entries here. Every `find` is checked to occur exactly once in its chapter before
The rule is unchanged: a sentence whose subject is the reader, the answer, the
paper or the material is not teaching the subject, and it goes; a sentence whose
subject is the subject stays. "Consider a replicated database system" keeps its
imperative - it is a worked example being set up, not an instruction to the reader.

edits.why: the three tiers are the fact; how to read them is not
edits.find: Read the tiers as a division of labour, not a diagram: the presentation tier
edits.to: The presentation tier

edits.why: the order of the three parts is a fact about the section, not an instruction
edits.find: Read them as one sequence: what a socket is, then what its two ends contain, then what a program that uses it looks like.
edits.to: The three parts are one sequence: what a socket is, then what its two ends contain, then what a program that uses it looks like.

edits.why: a heading that tells the reader what to do to a sentence instead of naming what the box is about
edits.find: Read that last sentence twice
edits.to: The requirement, and its limit

edits.why: the four properties divide a certain way, which is the claim
edits.find: Note how the four divide.
edits.to: The four divide into two kinds.

edits.why: the three message types are the content; what an answer should name is the marking
edits.find: Three message types, and an answer should name all three:
edits.to: Three message types:

edits.why: the trade is the fact; to state it in an answer is strategy
edits.find: That is the trade to state in an answer: message cost per entry
edits.to: That is the trade: message cost per entry

edits.why: the three rules really are one rule; the reader does not have to be told how to read them
edits.find: Read the three rules as one rule about messages:
edits.to: The three rules are one rule about messages:

edits.why: a closing instruction; the use cases are cited by name and number instead
edits.find: Read it, then add the use cases from 5.4.4.
edits.to: The use cases in 5.4.4 follow from the same comparison.

edits.why: where the trade is visible in the table is a fact about the table
edits.find: Read the table down a column rather than across a row, because the four models are four settings of one trade:
edits.to: Read down a column and the four models are four settings of one trade:

edits.why: a heading names the two properties; what students lose is about the marking
edits.find: Scalability versus elasticity — the distinction students lose
edits.to: Scalability versus elasticity

edits.why: how to draw it is the instruction; in an answer is the framing
edits.find: How to draw it in an answer
edits.to: How to draw it

edits.why: the two lookups are the reason, which is a fact about memory virtualization
edits.find: If a question asks why memory virtualization costs performance, that is the answer — two lookups where a physical machine does one —
edits.to: Memory virtualization costs performance because of two lookups where a physical machine does one —

edits.why: the same function one layer apart is the fact; what satisfies a mark scheme is about the marking
edits.find: Say both sentences and the mark scheme is satisfied: the same function, one layer apart.
edits.to: The two are the same function, one layer apart.

edits.why: an instruction about answering, where naming the service is what matters
edits.find: Write the full name in any answer.
edits.to: The full name is the pattern: the same three services appear under whichever vendor's label.

edits.why: the analogy is about the customer, not about the reader
edits.find: Take and bake: the vendor delivers the dough, sauce, toppings and cheese; you supply the table, oven and fire.
edits.to: Take and bake: the vendor supplies the dough, sauce, toppings and cheese; the customer supplies the table, oven and fire.

edits.why: a table label names who manages what, and the second party is the customer
edits.find: You manage the operating system, runtime and application;
edits.to: Customer manages the operating system, runtime and application;

edits.why: two of the five being about cost is the observation; telling the reader to notice it is not
edits.find: Notice that only two of the five are about speed.
edits.to: Only two of the five are about speed.

edits.why: the number is the point, and the sentence can make it without instructing the reader
edits.find: Learn one number to make the availability row mean something.
edits.to: One number makes the availability row mean something.

edits.why: the sentence is about the second rule and about what turns a list into an answer
edits.find: That is exactly the exercise the second rule asks for — consider the impact of the cloud on each phase — and it is what turns a list of seven words into an answer.

edits.why: a column heading names the column; an answer is the paper's business
edits.find: <th>The one-line definition for an answer</th>
edits.to: <th>The one-line definition</th>

edits.why: the caption should say what the figure shows, not what it answers
edits.find: That chain is the answer to "how do containers and orchestration support cloud-native architecture".

edits.why: the sentence carries the subject; that it is the one to write in an answer is framing
edits.find: In an answer about cloud-native architecture, one sentence carries it:
edits.to: One sentence carries cloud-native architecture:

edits.why: the two roles are complementary, and what half an answer needs is not a fact about the tools
edits.find: Because the course's syllabus pairs them in one sub-topic, an answer that gives only one of the two roles has answered half the question.
edits.to: The two roles are complementary, and one without the other describes half the pair.
